details.description: Ink-Whisper is Cartesia's lower-cost speech-to-text model, used for batch transcription of pre-recorded audio and, via Cartesia's manual-finalization realtime endpoint, for streaming transcription without built-in turn detection (the snapshot ink-whisper-2025-06-04 is documented as stable). Cartesia describes it as more accurate and lower-latency than baseline Whisper, with dynamic chunking for variable-length audio, resilience to background noise and telephony artifacts, and accurate transcription of proper nouns and domain-specific terms. Cartesia's current docs describe it as an older model and point users to Ink-2 for improved turn detection in English voice agents, though Ink-Whisper remains documented and available.
advantages: Cartesia reports higher accuracy and lower latency than baseline Whisper.
Supports transcription across around 99 languages, per Cartesia's documentation.
Dynamic chunking handles variable-length audio and interruptions.
Designed for resilience to background noise and telephony artifacts, with accurate transcription of proper nouns and domain-specific terminology.
disadvantages: Not available on Cartesia's auto-finalization realtime endpoint with native turn detection, which is exclusive to Ink-2 and Ink-preview; Ink-Whisper is used via the batch endpoint or the manual-finalization realtime endpoint instead.
Cartesia's own docs describe it as an older model and direct users toward Ink-2, which offers improved turn detection for English voice agents.
No word-error-rate figures, diarization support, or domain-specific (e.g. medical, phonecall) tuning are documented for this model.
use_cases: Batch transcription of pre-recorded audio files.
Multilingual transcription where broad language coverage matters more than realtime turn detection.
Lower-cost transcription workloads that do not need Ink-2's realtime turn-detection features.

notes: Cartesia's docs page states this model supports '99 languages' but the enumerated list on the same page contains 100 names ending in Cantonese, which matches the well-known discrepancy in Whisper-derived models (the original 99-language list plus Cantonese added later); I listed every name given rather than trim one to force the count to 99. No WER, diarization, or domain-tuning (medical/phonecall) details were found on the maker's page for this specific model, so I left those out rather than assume they carry over from the general Ink product page. Verify pass: the compare-endpoints table and the /stt/websocket API reference's model enum (ink-2, ink-preview, ink-whisper) show Ink-Whisper also works on the manual-finalization realtime endpoint, not just batch; only the auto-finalization/turn-detection endpoint is Ink-2-exclusive.
